newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola futures end down on late fund selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola futures end down on late fund selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on late fund selling and commission selling, traders said.

"The funds sold 150 to 200 July at the end of the day," a trader said. Commission houses were the best sellers as UGG bought nearby and Cargill bought November. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -7.05 Tuesday from -11.02 Monday. About 300 July-Nov spread at $37, May-July $2, Aug-Nov $38. Volume was 5,975 lots, or 119,500 tonnes, with 265 hedges.
Japan bought 3,000-4,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
May canola fell $1.30 to $422, July slipped $1 to $424.60 and November was up $0.60 at $388.40.
"StatsCan's report was a factor in the wheat early in the day but we firmed up on the U.S. corn," a grain trader said.
In its stocks report early Tuesday, Statistics Canada put wheat stocks as of March 31 at 19.3 million tonnes -- a figure considered bearish by some traders.
July feed wheat futures closed $0.50 lower at $159.90 and October fell $0.40 to $162.50 on commercial liquidation, hedges. Volume was 1,142.
July western barley rose $0.30 to $135.90 on commission buying as UGG sold, traders said.
July feed peas up US$1 to US$202, October fell US$1 to US$192.50 on two-way commercial trade. Oats did not trade.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
